Subject: Rate card and volume discount inquiry

Hi Karthik —

We're evaluating Redwood for our next-gen data enrichment pipeline and expecting bursty high-volume needs. Rough projection: ~1B tokens/month by Q4 with spikes up to 200M tokens/day for short campaigns. Before we spin up a PoC, can you share: a) your baseline hosted API rate card b) typical volume discount tiers (committed vs. on-demand) and c) any prepay/true-up mechanics?

We also have a few compliance questions but can follow up separately. Would appreciate a starter rate card or sample pricing matrix we can run internally.

Thanks,
Claire Jensen
Head of Platform Integrations
DataWave Inc.

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the note and the projection — that's helpful. At a high level for hosted API:

- Baseline (on-demand): $0.004 per 1K tokens for text-generation endpoints.
- Volume tiers (committed monthly): we typically offer tiered discounts based on committed monthly tokens (examples below).
- True-up / overage: we allow monthly true-ups; overages billed at the lower committed tier rate when you exceed the band consistently (we can define smoothing windows).

To give you a useful starter, can you confirm: 1) percentage split short-form vs. long-form (avg tokens/req), 2) expected 95th percentile daily peak, and 3) whether you need reserved capacity (low-latency SLOs) or can operate on shared hosted. Vanessa is cc'd to surface packaging options and a draft rate card.

I'll keep this high-level until we have your usage mix — happy to hop on a 30-min call.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Claire —

Following up with a starter draft rate card and packaging notes (attached). High-level packaging we recommend based on the projection you shared:

- Band A (0–250M tokens/mo): $0.0035 per 1K tokens (no commit)
- Band B (250M–750M tokens/mo): $0.0026 per 1K tokens (6–12 month commit, discount applies to tokens in band)
- Band C (750M+ tokens/mo): $0.0019 per 1K tokens (12+ month commit or reserved capacity)

Other notes:
- Reserved capacity option gives predictable latency and a +10% uplift on committed price (applies when you require dedicated pools).
- We support monthly true-up, with ability to ladder customers who go over threshold for >60 days.
- Prepay credits accepted, often used to smooth billing.

I've attached Draft_Rate_Card_v1.pdf and a simple banded example using the projection you mentioned. This is intentionally conservative — we can be flexible on the band boundaries and the effective blended rate for negotiation.

Attachments: Draft_Rate_Card_v1.pdf

Thanks Vanessa — the draft is exactly what we were hoping to see. A couple follow-ups so we can evaluate:

1) If we commit to a Band B level (e.g., 500M tokens/mo), how does overage behave? If we spike to 900M one month, do tokens above 750M automatically get billed at Band C rate or is there a buffer/true-up smoothing?

2) Are there minimum monthly monetary commitments or only token counts? We prefer a dollar-based commit for internal finance visibility.

3) On reserved capacity: curious what lead time and contract term you typically require for a dedicated pool.

If you can put those points in writing (and include a simple example invoice math), I can circulate with finance and procurement.

- Claire

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Rate card and volume discount inquiry — draft attached

Hi Claire —

Following up on Vanessa's draft and your questions: please see the concrete mechanics below and a worked example.

- Overage handling: We apply monthly true-up with a 30-day smoothing window. If a single calendar month exceeds the top boundary (750M) but average usage over the smoothing window stays within Band B, we bill the spike at a one-time overage at Band C rate for the excess. If elevated usage persists (>60 days), we automatically move the customer to the higher band for billing and discuss formal amendment.

- Dollar-based minimums: We can express commitments as either token counts or an equivalent $CPT (commitment in dollars). For example, a 500M token/month commit at Band B equates to a $1,300/mo commitment (500,000 * $0.0026). We’ll present both options in the SOW.

- Reserved capacity lead time: typical lead time is 4–6 weeks for capacity provisioning in hosted regions; for dedicated pools in a new region or private deployment this can be 8–12 weeks. Contract term for preferred pricing is usually 12 months.

Worked example (simplified):
- Committed: 500M tokens/mo at Band B ($0.0026/1K) -> monthly commitment = $1,300
- Month with spike: 900M tokens -> tokens above 750M = 150M tokens billed at Band C ($0.0019/1K) -> overage = 150,000 * $0.0019 = $285
- Invoice math: base invoice $1,300 + overage $285 = $1,585 for the month. If average across 60-day window stays above Band B, we ladder up the committed band and retro-adjust per contract terms.

I've attached the same Draft_Rate_Card_v1.pdf for reference. If this looks good, we can generate a simple SOW template and a DocuSign link to capture the commitment.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call tomorrow to run through numbers.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com
